entries.rule: Track and population fields: route is the route the drug was given by in the patients compared
entries.note: Goldenberg 2009 (PMID 18941114, epub 2008-10-21) quote verbatim; retro and year 2008 hold. The quoted patients got 'low intravenous or subcutaneous doses', so route should be mixed, not iv.
entries.adjudication_note: Fields rule (route = route in patients compared): status retro and 2008 hold; quoted patients got IV or SC doses, so route should be mixed, not iv. Field correction only; status unchanged.

entries.note: Morschhauser 2009 (PMID 19451441, epub 2009-05-18) quote verbatim; IV weekly infusions, 55/82 FL. Monkey data (Oct 2008) post-date rituximab and veltuzumab phase I depletion, so retro. NCT00285428 first posted 2006-02-02 confirmed.
Engelberts 2020 (PMID 31981978) quote verbatim; FDA review lines ~1977-1981 confirm SC lower Cmax/cytokines, comparable depletion.
Hutchings 2021 (PMID 34508654) quote verbatim; 48 mg RP2D, MTD not reached, no grade>=3 CRS. Whether an SC-route claim counts as a 'regimen target' is borderline (see rule questions).

Li 2022 (PMID 35996883, epub 2022-09-27) quote verbatim; fit to escalation data and published a year after Hutchings 2021 named 48 mg RP2D, though abstract says it 'guided selection of 48 mg'. Retrodiction status is a rule question.

entries.rule: Dose: target reached scores dose, not the later plateau analysis; rule 6 dating (as adjudicated earlier on this entry)
entries.note: Sinnollareddy 2026 (PMID 42541678) quote verbatim; retro supported (Li 2022 fit to escalation data after 48-mg RP2D). Year stays at 2026 against the adjudicated dating: dose scores target reached, FL cohort dosed to 48 mg in Linton 2024.
entries.adjudication_note: Dose table (target reached scores dose) and rule 6: retro holds; year should date to first public FL dosing to 48 mg after Li 2022 (Linton 2024, or an earlier congress abstract), not the 2026 plateau analysis.

entries.note: Stein 2004 (PMID 15102696) quote verbatim; abstract adds 'expected that in humans IMMU-106 should be at least as effective as rituximab'.

NCT00285428 primary outcome 'Safety and tolerance of different dose levels', first posted 2006-02-02, confirmed; FL ORR 44% (24/55) quote verbatim but secondary, so untested under the single-arm ruling.
Engelberts 2020 quote verbatim; humanized-mouse models were non-FL lines/PDX (FDA review).
van der Horst 2021 (PMID 33602901, Feb 2021) quote verbatim; FL n=15, irrespective of prior CD20 mAb.
Li 2022 quote verbatim; FDA review (line ~9124) also describes model built on preclinical plus escalation data.

Linton 2024 (PMID 38889737) quote verbatim; ORR is the cohort's primary endpoint. AbbVie release 2023-06-27 confirmed (IRC ORR 82%, above prespecified threshold), so year 2023. Model Jan 2020 post-dates rituximab FL results: retro.
Same Linton quote and 2023-06-27 topline release confirmed; eligibility required prior anti-CD20. Ex-vivo data (Feb 2021) post-date rituximab/mosunetuzumab FL responses, so retro.

Same Linton quote and 2023 release; Li 2022 abstract confirms model fit to escalation patient data and predicts 48 mg 'may achieve optimal response rates' in FL. Retro supported; low confidence appropriate.
Quote verbatim in FDA BLA 761324 multidisciplinary review (bundle txt line 1978-1979); tier 2 correct; dated to Engelberts 2020.

entries.rule: Dating (6): year is the earliest public date, congress abstract included
entries.note: Hutchings 2021 quote verbatim; retro holds. But epcoritamab CRS (59%, all Gr 1/2) was public in ASCO 2020 abstract 8009 (J Clin Oncol 38 suppl, May 2020), after Engelberts Jan 2020, so the comparison dates to 2020.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 6 (congress abstract counts): retro holds; ASCO 2020 abstract 8009 (JCO 38:15_suppl 8009) already reported CRS 59%, all grade 1/2, after Engelberts Jan 2020, so year should be 2020.

entries.note: Shi 2024 (PMC11245993) intro sentence on Daudi nude-mouse regression, equal to obinutuzumab, found verbatim; summary only, no figures or citation. Opening untested at 2019 proxy (first MIL62 trials) is acceptable.

entries.rule: Dating (6): record registry_date; the registry lookup is mandatory
entries.note: Shi 2024 (PMC11245993) quote verbatim; paper's primary endpoint ORR met (registry lists CR rate). Combination ruling plus same-target retrodiction gives retro. registry_date null; NCT04110301 first posted 2019-10-01.
entries.adjudication_note: Combination ruling plus retrodiction: retro holds; rule 6/9 mandatory registry lookup: registry_date should be 2019-10-01 (NCT04110301 first posted). No registry results, so year stays 2024.

entries.note: FDA BLA 761324 review p.57: ProStorm soluble whole-blood assay (study 32318, non-GLP) quote verbatim. Not reported in Engelberts 2020 (monkey cytokines only), so first public 2023; 2017 opening proxy fine.

Hutchings 2021 quote verbatim; whole-blood assay first public in the 2023 FDA BLA 761324 review, after epcoritamab CRS in patients (ASCO 2020, Lancet 2021), so retro under the post-dating ruling; year 2023 correct.

Engelberts 2020 (PMID 31981978, epub 2020-01-23) quote verbatim; valid untested opener of the epcoritamab SC track on the shared cyno model_id; untested_reason not required as eng 4 is the track's latest entry.

Hutchings 2021 (PMID 34508654, epub 2021-09-08) quote verbatim; SC route, mixed B-NHL with FL subset. Rituximab B-cell depletion predates the 2020 monkey paper, so retro. ASCO 2020 abstract 8009 does not report B-cell depletion; 2021 stands.

missing: Veltuzumab phase I/II registry records NCT00285428 (start 2004-09, primary: safety/tolerance) and NCT00596804; the draft says the registry record was not located.

FDA BLA 761324 multidisciplinary review (2023) exposure-response: 'TMDD saturation was observed starting from 48 mg, due to a plateau in tumor killing' with full doses >48 mg not expected to add efficacy. This is an earlier public dose comparison than Sinnollareddy 2026, though in LBCL.

Goldenberg 2009 (doi:10.1182/blood-2008-07-168146) abstract states mouse/monkey findings 'are consistent with activity in patients with NHL given low intravenous or subcutaneous doses', which makes it a comparison_stated source, possibly a retrodiction.

MIL62: phase 1b/2 with lenalidomide in R/R FL/MZL (eClinicalMedicine 2024, sciencedirect pii S2589537024002815) and phase 3 NCT04834024 (MIL62+len vs len, PFS primary, status unknown, no results). No MIL62 preclinical model track was searched; any MIL62 xenograft paper would be its own track.

Imvotamab (IGM-2323): NCT04082936 terminated for 'Strategic Pipeline Prioritization' (not efficacy); phase 1 data only as meeting abstracts (e.g. EHA 2022 P1276, PMC9429641). No efficacy failure to add, but the context note could cite the termination reason.

MIL62 monotherapy phase I/II NCT04103905 in CD20+ NHL incl. FL/MZL (Shi 2024, eClinicalMedicine doi:10.1016/j.eclinm.2024.102702, reports ORR 'similar to obinutuzumab', FL data unpublished): the monotherapy test of the Daudi xenograft track once published.
rule_questions: Does a model's route recommendation (monkey SC vs IV lowers cytokine peaks with equal depletion) count as a 'regimen target' for dose, when humans were never dosed IV for comparison? The draft scores it same; the alternative is untested/no_prediction.

Is an in-silico PBPK/PD model fit to the same trial's escalation data, published after that trial named the 48 mg RP2D but said to have guided the choice, a retrodiction for dose (retro) and prospective for the later pivotal FL cohort's efficacy?

When the dose 'same' depends only on the target being reached, does the entry date to when FL patients were dosed to target (Linton 2024) or to when a later analysis confirmed the plateau the model stated (Sinnollareddy 2026)?
